prompt: Some people believe that money is one of the most important factors in a person's happiness. To what extent do you agree withh this?
essay:
In today's capitalistic world, wealth is often considered the main contributor to happiness. Even though money matters, I agree with this view to a limited extent, and I will elaborate on my point in this essay.

To begin with, individuals need money to cover their basic necessities, such as housing, rent, and bills. If they are not able to support their family financially, they definitely feel guilty and miserable. Furthermore, a human being tends to improve their standards of living, such as purchasing a modern house or a luxurious car, travelling abroad, or studying overseas. These actions, which require a great deal of money, make people happy and satisfied with their lives. Thus, being wealthy is a privilege at some points in life.

Even so, there are several other considerations that can outweigh wealth. Firstly, without physical and mental health, people cannot be fully content. If a person has a serious illness, he most likely spends the money on his health, instead of the things that bring happiness. Secondly, job satisfaction also plays an important role. Doing a job that does not align with their inner values, people might feel overwhelmed, even if they are paid well. As a result, they might become anxious and stressed, even get into depression, which deteriorates their relationship with their families and friends.  Therefore, money does not guarantee genuine happiness.

In conclusion, although money can guarantee a comfortable lifestyle and overall satisfaction to some extent, I firmly believe that real happiness comes from overall well-being, a contented family and fulfilling work.
